pharm: Time-dependent bactericidal glycopeptide active against Gram-positive organisms including MRSA; given IV for systemic infection and orally for C. difficile (oral form not systemically absorbed).
quick: IV 15-20 mg/kg q8-12h (or 500 mg q6h / 1 g q12h); oral 125 mg q6h for C. diff
Use only if clearly needed; appears low risk
Caution; excreted in milk, poor oral absorption
Dose/interval adjusted by CrCl and levels
summary: Vancomycin is a glycopeptide antibiotic for serious Gram-positive infections, especially methicillin-resistant staphylococci (MRSA), and for penicillin-allergic patients or those failing other drugs. Given by slow IV infusion for systemic infection (rapid infusion causes 'vancomycin infusion reaction' / red-man syndrome). The oral capsule is used for Clostridioides difficile colitis and is not appreciably absorbed. It is nephrotoxic at higher exposures and requires therapeutic drug monitoring (trough or AUC-guided) and renal dose adjustment. Infuse over at least 60 minutes at no more than 10 mg/min.
indications: Serious or severe infections caused by methicillin-resistant (beta-lactam-resistant) staphylococci
Treatment in penicillin-allergic patients or those who cannot take/failed other drugs
Septicemia, bone infections, lower respiratory tract infections, skin and skin-structure infections
Endocarditis caused by S. viridans or S. bovis (alone or with an aminoglycoside)
Enterococcal endocarditis (in combination with an aminoglycoside)
Prosthetic-valve endocarditis caused by S. epidermidis or diphtheroids (with rifampin and/or aminoglycoside)
Oral vancomycin: Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea/pseudomembranous colitis (oral form, separate labeling)

dosage.t: 500 mg every 6 h or 1 g every 12 h
dosage.n: Each dose over >=60 min at <=10 mg/min; weight-based 15-20 mg/kg q8-12h is common modern practice
Target AUC/MIC or trough per guideline; consider loading dose 25-30 mg/kg in critically ill
Each dose over >=60 min; monitor serum levels

dosage.t: Every 12 h (1st week of life), every 8 h thereafter to 1 month
dosage.n: Longer intervals in premature infants; monitor levels closely
Oral form; minimal systemic absorption (separate labeling)
Greater reductions may be needed in premature infants and the elderly

admin: Infuse IV over at least 60 minutes; do not exceed 10 mg/min to reduce infusion reactions
Use a concentration of no more than 5 mg/mL (up to 10 mg/mL only if fluid-restricted, higher infusion-reaction risk)
Do not give IM; not absorbed adequately by mouth for systemic infection
Oral capsules/solution are reserved for C. difficile colitis
Ensure adequate hydration; monitor renal function during therapy
Avoid concurrent nephrotoxic/ototoxic drugs where possible
moa: Inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis by binding with high affinity to the D-alanyl-D-alanine terminus of peptidoglycan precursors, blocking transglycosylation and transpeptidation; it also alters cell-membrane permeability and RNA synthesis. Bactericidal against susceptible aerobic Gram-positive organisms.
preg: Animal reproduction studies have not been conducted; vancomycin crosses the placenta. In a limited study, no fetal sensorineural hearing loss or nephrotoxicity attributable to vancomycin was noted. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: Excreted in human milk; because oral absorption by the infant is poor, systemic effects are unlikely, but exercise caution and weigh the importance of the drug to the mother.
renal: Dose adjustment is required in renal impairment - reduce the dose or extend the interval based on CrCl and serum levels. Greater reductions may be needed in premature infants and the elderly. Renal excretion is the major route; monitor renal function and levels closely.

major: Other nephrotoxic/ototoxic drugs (aminoglycosides, amphotericin B, polymyxin B/colistin, cisplatin, viomycin, bacitracin) - additive toxicity
Piperacillin-tazobactam (associated with increased risk of acute kidney injury when combined)
moderate: Anesthetic agents (erythema, histamine-like flushing, anaphylactoid reactions)
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor serum vancomycin levels (trough or AUC-guided dosing) and serial renal function.

common: Infusion-related flushing of upper body ('red-man'/vancomycin infusion reaction)
serious: Ototoxicity (hearing loss, usually with high levels or renal dysfunction)
rare: DRESS syndrome and other severe cutaneous reactions (SJS/TEN, AGEP, linear IgA bullous dermatosis)
emergency: Severe infusion reaction with hypotension/cardiac arrest (rapid infusion)

monitoring: Serum vancomycin levels - trough or AUC-guided (e.g., AUC/MIC 400-600 for serious MRSA infection)
Renal function (serum creatinine, urine output) at baseline and during therapy
Audiometry/hearing in prolonged therapy or high levels
CBC for neutropenia/thrombocytopenia with prolonged use
Infusion rate and signs of infusion reaction
counsel: This antibiotic is given slowly into a vein over at least an hour to prevent flushing and a drop in blood pressure
Report flushing, rash, itching, or breathlessness during the infusion
Report any change in hearing, ringing in the ears, or reduced urination
Oral vancomycin (for C. difficile) is taken by mouth and works in the gut - complete the full course
Stay well hydrated and inform staff of any kidney problems or other ear/kidney-affecting medicines
pk: ~4-6 h (normal renal function); markedly prolonged in renal impairment
Based on dosing interval; ~80-90% renally excreted unchanged
Reconstituted/IV: per labeling; vials at 20-25 C before reconstitution
pearls: Infuse over >=60 min at <=10 mg/min - rapid infusion causes the histamine-mediated 'red-man'/infusion reaction (not a true allergy)
Modern dosing is AUC-guided (target AUC/MIC 400-600 for serious MRSA); troughs >15-20 increase nephrotoxicity
Oral vancomycin is NOT absorbed and treats C. difficile colitis - do not use IV for gut C. diff
Combination with piperacillin-tazobactam raises AKI risk - monitor renal function closely
Poorly removed by conventional hemodialysis; high-flux membranes and hemoperfusion can enhance clearance
Synergistic with aminoglycosides for enterococcal endocarditis but adds nephrotoxicity
missed: Hospital-administered; give as soon as noted and adjust the schedule, then recheck levels if timing changed. Do not double the dose. For oral C. diff therapy, take the missed dose when remembered unless near the next dose.
overdose: Provide supportive care with maintenance of glomerular filtration. Vancomycin is poorly removed by conventional dialysis; hemofiltration and hemoperfusion with polysulfone/resin can increase clearance. Monitor renal and auditory function and serum levels.
